title: Normal driving, no faults
about: Catch-up: car 1 starts 36 m behind the leader and the platoon has to close up smoothly. With only their own radar and no messages, the cars crash at 11 s.

title: Leader brakes at 30 s
about: The leader slows from 15 to 8 m/s in about 5 s and speeds up again. Without messages the platoon has already crashed at 11 s.

title: Messages arrive 0.5 s late
about: Every V2V message arrives 5 steps late, and each car uses the newest (old) value it has.

title: Messages 0.5 s late, radar fallback
about: Same delay, but a car estimates the front car's speed from its own radar instead of trusting an old message. NeurComm's other message parts (policy, hidden state) cannot be estimated.

title: Half of all messages lost
about: Each V2V message is lost with probability 50%; a car reuses the last value it received.

title: Car 4 crashes at 25 s, then the leader brakes
about: Car 4's process goes silent (crash-stop). The road detects it with a timeout and the car rolls on at constant speed, so it cannot brake when the leader does.

title: Car 4 is malicious, no defence
about: From 25 s car 4 drives normally but sends random values (Byzantine fault: it keeps talking, but lies). The leader brakes at 30 s and the cars behind car 4 believe its messages.

title: Car 4 is malicious, radar check on
about: Same attack. Every car compares its front car's claimed speed with what its own radar says (how fast the gap changes) and ignores messages that disagree by more than 2 m/s.
